title: api-config-shape-draft-jamie
content:
Quick scratchpad for API + config shape. Trying to capture a minimal, ergonomic shape that maps to: hosted API (simple), dedicated/private (more knobs), and runtime (batches/KV/cache/profile).

High-level goals:
- Single config object that can be partial (defaults in control plane).
- Clear separation: request-level hints vs route-level defaults vs runtime constraints.
- Support for model variants + fallback policies.
- Easy to express batching/caching intent without exposing internal runtime plumbing.

Notes/assumptions:
- Most users will only use hosted API and want minimal surface area. Advanced users (Dedicated/Private) will override more fields.
- Route config should be versioned and pin model revisions.
- Runtime accepts 'runtime_profile' strings that map to precompiled kernel variants (e.g., low-latency, cost-opt).

Sketch: top-level keys and short descriptions (pseudo-spec as plain text to keep this a scratchpad)
- name: string (route identifier)
- model: name, version, variant (allow list or single)
- defaults: max_tokens, temperature, top_p (route defaults)
- request_hints: list/string accepted from API caller to override small things
- routing_policy: region_preference, fallbacks, priority
- batching: enabled, max_batch_size, max_wait_ms
- kv_cache: enabled, scope (session|global), eviction_policy
- quant_profile: string (suggested quantization level)
- runtime_profile: string (low-latency | cost-optimized | high-throughput)
- observability: sample_rate, trace

Example (pseudo-json as a doc snippet, included inline):

{
  "name": "chat-support-route-v1",
  "model": { "name": "redwood-7b", "version": "2025-01-10", "variant": "int8" },
  "defaults": { "max_tokens": 512, "temperature": 0.0 },
  "routing_policy": { "region_preference": ["us-west1", "us-east1"], "fallbacks": ["redwood-7b-quantized"], "priority": "latency" },
  "batching": { "enabled": true, "max_batch_size": 32, "max_wait_ms": 15 },
  "kv_cache": { "enabled": true, "scope": "session", "eviction_policy": "lru" },
  "runtime_profile": "low-latency",
  "observability": { "sample_rate": 0.05, "trace": true }
}

Open questions / TODOs:
- How much of this should be writable by end users vs admin-only? (e.g., runtime_profile might be restricted)
- Do we expose explicit kernel/cuda flags? better to keep opaque and map them via profiles.
- Batching defaults: should hosted API always enforce a ceiling (e.g., max_batch_size <= 16) to avoid noisy neighbor issues?
- KV cache visibility: do we return cache-hit metadata to callers for debugging? (useful, but maybe leaking internals)

Edge cases:
- If batching.enabled=false but runtime wants to batch for efficiency, we need a way for runtime to override with safe bounds and a notice flag.
- Model fallback: when fallback kicks in, should we rewrite model name in logs/response headers? (transparency vs UX)

Diagrams as text (very rough):

Client -> API Gateway (auth, rate limit) -> Route config lookup -> Router: apply routing_policy -> Select pool (hosted/dedicated/private) -> Runtime (apply runtime_profile, batching, kv) -> Model backends (primary -> fallback) -> Response (headers: x-rw-model, x-rw-cache-hit)

Conversations / session handling:
- session_id provided by client. KV cache scoped to session by default.
- TTL per-session configurable at route level.

Telemetry / rollback hooks:
- Route config should allow 'canary' boolean and traffic_split to support gradual rollouts.
- Metric set: latency_p50/p90, token_cost_per_req, cache_hit_rate, error_rate.
- Automatic rollback if model's quality regresses on eval set tied to the route.

Developer ergonomics (API surface):
- Minimal route create/update API: name + model + defaults + optional knobs.
- Advanced API: accept full config YAML/JSON for Dedicated/Private.
- CLI helper to diff configs and show runtime-mapped profiles.

Action items (next steps):
- Align with runtime team on runtime_profile semantics and safe overrides (ask: Casey Lin + infra).
- Decide which fields are admin-only (security/ops).
- Wire up simple create-route UI mock in Console (low priority).
- Draft a small POST /routes API proposal (include examples for hosted vs dedicated).

Scratch / random thoughts:
- Might be nice to have a tiny 'tuning hint' field where users can input high-level goals: "minimize_cost"|"minimize_latency" to let control plane pick batch/quant/profile automatically.
- 'observability.sample_rate' could be percent string to make UI simpler ("5%")

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc messy — will refine into PRD once runtime_profile semantics are finalized.
- Ping Samir about fallback transparency policy.

End of scratchpad.
